source: ICH E2A 'Clinical Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting' (1994) §II.B for the seriousness criteria; 21 CFR 312.32(c) for the sponsor's 7-day (fatal or life-threatening unexpected suspected adverse reactions) and 15-day (other serious unexpected) IND safety reporting clocks. The 24-hour site-to-sponsor window is the common protocol-level obligation ('within 24 hours of the site becoming aware') and is configurable here.
rationale: A 'yes' to the hospital/ER gate meets the ICH E2A seriousness criterion 'requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation', so Interim marks seriousness as SUSPECTED (never decided; the investigator decides) and starts the site clock at the moment the site became aware, which is the check-in completion time. The sponsor-side clocks are shown as informational downstream deadlines; they are owned by the sponsor's pharmacovigilance process, not by this system. The clock stops only when an investigator records a seriousness decision.

informational_sponsor_clocks.note: Informational only. Computed from site awareness; owned by the sponsor, not by Interim.

clock_alerts.note: A running 24 h site-to-sponsor clock pages the on-call role once when 4 h remain (clock.due_soon) and once when it passes due (clock.breached). Sites set their own lead time.
